_provenance: Curated by parallel agents against RCSB REST/FASTA + JASPAR + primary literature; see notes per entry. Sequences taken verbatim from RCSB FASTA, not reconstructed.

controls.label: Zif268
controls.motif_source: JASPAR MA0162.5 (EGR1, CORE, 10 bp; PFM consensus ACGCCCACGC on the opposite strand = GCGTGGGCGT). Primary structure paper: Elrod-Erickson M, Rould MA, Nekludova L, Pabo CO, "Zif268 protein-DNA complex refined at 1.6 A: a model system for understanding zinc finger-DNA interactions," Structure 4:1171-1180 (1996). Original: Pavletich & Pabo, Science 252:809 (1991).
controls.notes:
VERIFIED: 1AAY exists, title "ZIF268 ZINC FINGER-DNA COMPLEX", X-ray 1.6 A. Three entities: protein auth chain A (entity 3, "PROTEIN (ZIF268 ZINC FINGER PEPTIDE)", Mus musculus 10090) plus two DNA strands, auth B = 5'-AGCGTGGGCGT-3' and auth C = 5'-TACGCCCACGC-3'. Sequence above was taken verbatim from the RCSB FASTA for entry 1AAY, not from memory. Note auth/label chain IDs are swapped in the FASTA (label chain C = auth A); the protein is auth chain A.

MOTIF: consensus and crystallised site AGREE. JASPAR MA0162.5 argmax consensus is ACGCCCACGC; its reverse complement GCGTGGGCGT is exactly the strand-B sequence minus the 5' A. The classic 9-bp Zif268 site GCG TGG GCG (one 3-bp subsite per finger) is contained within it. Reported here as the 10-mer sense strand matching the crystal; trim to GCGTGGGCG if a strictly 9-bp three-finger site is wanted. Duplex is not blunt: strands are 11-mers that pair over 10 bp with single-nucleotide 5' overhangs at both ends, so a naive duplex built from the deposited sequences will have unpaired termini.

CONFOUNDS / CAVEATS for use as a control:
1. ZINC DEPENDENCE — this is the big one. The entry contains 3 Zn2+ ions (12 metal-coordination bonds), one per C2H2 finger. The betabetaalpha fold does not exist without them. If the AF3-class predictor is run protein+DNA only, with no Zn ligands supplied, the fold and hence any PAE-derived interface metric may be degraded for reasons unrelated to sequence specificity. Supply 3 Zn as ligands, or note the omission explicitly.
2. BASICITY — the peptide is arginine/lysine-rich (net charge strongly positive; R/K in every recognition helix, plus the C-terminal RQKD tail). Specificity is real and well characterised (Arg/Asp/His major-groove base contacts), but the protein will also have appreciable nonspecific electrostatic affinity for any duplex, so a scrambled-DNA negative control will not necessarily score as "non-binding".
3. Reads the MAJOR groove via three tandem recognition helices — the intended, canonical mode. Good.
4. Monomeric single-chain domain; no obligate oligomerisation, so a 1:1 protein:duplex prediction is physically correct. Good.
5. Species mismatch between structure and motif: the deposited peptide is murine Zif268 (Egr1) while MA0162.5 is human EGR1. The three recognition helices are identical between mouse and human, so the motif transfers, but flag it if strict species matching matters.
6. Construct is an isolated engineered zinc-finger peptide (residues ~333-421 of Egr1), not full-length EGR1; some N-/C-terminal residues in the FASTA entity are disordered/unmodelled in the coordinates (entry reports 107 total modelled monomers across all three polymers). Use the FASTA sequence as input but expect a few flexible terminal residues with high PAE that could dilute a whole-chain PAE average — prefer interface-restricted PAE.
7. Zif268 is arguably the single most-studied protein-DNA complex and is heavily represented in the PDB (many engineered variants), so it is near-certainly in the predictor's training set. It is a strong positive control but a weak test of generalisation.

controls.label: LambdaRep
controls.motif_source: DNA as crystallised in PDB 1LMB (entities 1 and 2, auth chains 1/2: 5'-TATATCACCGCCAGTGGTAT-3' / 5'-AATACCACTGGCGGTGATAT-3'), 17-bp OL1 operator core. Primary citation: Beamer LJ & Pabo CO, "Refined 1.8 A crystal structure of the lambda repressor-operator complex", J Mol Biol 1992. No JASPAR matrix exists for lambda CI (JASPAR API search returns count=0; JASPAR covers eukaryotic TFs only).
controls.notes:
VERIFIED: 1LMB exists and is as claimed — "REFINED 1.8 ANGSTROM CRYSTAL STRUCTURE OF THE LAMBDA REPRESSOR-OPERATOR COMPLEX", protein/nucleic-acid complex, 1 protein entity (auth chains 3, 4) + 2 DNA entities (auth chains 1, 2). Sequence above is verbatim from https://www.rcsb.org/fasta/entry/1LMB (entity 1LMB_3), not reconstructed. UniProt P03034 (repressor CI), no engineered mutations; this is the N-terminal DNA-binding domain only (PDB residues 1-92 = P03034 residues 2-93, i.e. Met1 removed); full-length CI is 236 aa.

CONFOUNDS, in rough order of severity:
1. OBLIGATE DIMER / EFFECTIVE HALF-SITE. CI binds the 17-bp operator as a 2-fold-related dimer, each monomer inserting its HTH recognition helix into one half-site of the pseudo-palindrome. A single 92-mer chain paired with the full 17-bp duplex is half a biological complex: the monomer specifically reads only ~8 bp (TATCACCGC-type half-site), leaving the other half unengaged. If the pipeline folds one chain against the full duplex, the PAE metric is measuring a half-site interaction and may look worse than a genuine 1:1 specific binder. Options: model the duplex with two copies of chain 3, or accept that this entry is a half-site control and note it.
2. NO INTRINSIC DIMERISATION MODULE. The C-terminal dimerisation domain (residues ~132-236) is absent from 1LMB; the isolated NTD dimerises only weakly and largely operator-mediated. So even a 2:1 model has a weak, DNA-templated interface — the monomer fold itself is fine and stable in isolation (unlike a true obligate intertwined dimer), which mitigates (1) somewhat.
3. BASIC, FLEXIBLE N-TERMINAL ARM. Residues 1-6 (S-T-K-K-K-P) are a Lys-rich arm that wraps around the DNA and reaches the major groove on the far face; Lys4 makes a specific contact but the arm is also a generic electrostatic anchor and is conformationally labile / partly poorly ordered in the crystal. Expect elevated PAE for residues 1-6 regardless of specificity, and expect this arm to give nonzero affinity for arbitrary DNA. The chain overall is quite basic (7 K in the first 27 residues), so some nonspecific stickiness is expected.
4. MOTIF DEFINITION IS SOFT. There is no PWM/JASPAR entry. The 17-bp site is an imperfect dyad with a "consensus half" (TATCACCGC) and a "non-consensus half"; OL1 and OR1 are the two highest-affinity natural sites and differ from each other and from the six-site family. The reported motif is the actual crystallised OL1 core, which is the safest choice for a structure-prediction control (crystallised site == consensus half-site + natural non-consensus half). A fully symmetrised "consensus operator" (TATCACCGC + GCGGTGATA) is a different sequence used in some studies (e.g. Cro/CI comparison work) and is NOT what 1LMB contains.
5. DNA construct details: each strand is a 20-mer with 1-nt 5' overhangs (not blunt), so the deposited duplex is longer than the 17-bp site and staggered. Flanking bases TA.../...AT are crystallisation scaffolding, not part of the recognition site.
6. Recognition mode is the textbook favourable case — major-groove readout by an HTH (helix 2/3, ~residues 33-52), plus phosphate-backbone contacts from the arm. Not a minor-groove or indirect-readout reader, so it is a reasonable positive control on that axis.

controls.label: MAX_bHLH
controls.motif_source: JASPAR MA0058.3 (MAX, CORE vertebrates; PFM positions 3-8 are invariant C-A-C-G-T-G, flanks degenerate; same core in MA0058.1/.2/.4). Primary structure paper: Ferre-D'Amare AR, Prendergast GC, Ziff EB, Burley SK. "Recognition by Max of its cognate DNA through a dimeric b/HLH/Z domain." Nature 363:38-45 (1993).
controls.notes:
VERIFIED. 1AN2 exists and is as claimed: "Recognition by Max of its cognate DNA through a dimeric b/HLH/Z domain", X-ray, 2.9 A, protein/nucleic-acid complex. Asymmetric unit holds ONE protein chain (label_asym B, auth A; 86 aa, UniProt P61244 human MAX) and ONE DNA strand (label_asym A, auth B): 5'-GTGTAGGTCACGTGACCTACAC-3', which is self-complementary, so the duplex and the protein dimer are both generated by the crystallographic 2-fold. Biological assembly 1 = 4 chains (2 protein + 2 DNA), global C2.

E-box CONFIRMED: the crystallised 22-mer contains CACGTG at its centre, and this is identical to the JASPAR consensus core, so there is no crystal-vs-consensus discrepancy. Motif is a palindrome; each MAX monomer reads one CAC half-site via major-groove contacts (Glu32/Arg35-equivalent basic-region residues) - i.e. the 6-mer given here is the full dimeric site, NOT a half-site.

CONFOUNDS / CAVEATS for use as a control:
1. Obligate dimer. This is a b/HLH/Zip domain: the C-terminal ~30 residues (roughly M53-S86 here) are a leucine-zipper coiled coil that only exists as a parallel two-stranded dimer. A single-chain prediction is physically meaningless - the zipper helix has no hydrophobic partner and specific DNA binding requires both basic regions. If the pipeline folds one chain + duplex DNA, this entry will look artefactually bad for reasons unrelated to specificity. Strongly recommend supplying 2 identical protein chains + both DNA strands. I have reported one chain as instructed, but flag this as the single biggest risk for this entry.
2. DNA must be supplied as two strands. The deposited entity is one 22-mer; you must duplicate it (self-complementary) to build the duplex.
3. Basic and charged. Net charge approx +6 at neutral pH (19 Arg/Lys vs 13 Asp/Glu, plus 6 His), with a contiguous basic region (KRAHHNALERKRRDH) that is the DNA-reading element. Like all bHLH/bZIP proteins it retains measurable non-specific electrostatic affinity for any duplex DNA, so a ΔPAE-type specificity metric may show a non-zero floor on scrambled DNA. This is intrinsic to the family, not a defect of this particular entry.
4. Homodimer motif only. MA0058 describes MAX homodimer; MAX also heterodimerises with MYC/MAD (JASPAR MA0059 MAX::MYC) on the same CACGTG core, so the motif is not unique to MAX - fine for a specificity control, but do not treat CACGTG as MAX-diagnostic.
5. Flanking-base dependence. Positions 1-2 and 9-10 of MA0058.3 are degenerate but not uniform (mild preference for A/C 5' of the core); the crystal flanks GGTCACGTGACC are a strong-affinity context. Using the bare 6-mer padded with arbitrary flanks is acceptable but changes affinity somewhat.
6. Modest resolution (2.9 A) and the DNA is reported bent in the complex; side-chain and backbone detail is less reliable than in higher-resolution E-box structures (e.g. later MAX/MYC-MAX entries) if you need per-contact ground truth.

controls.label: Engrailed
controls.motif_source: JASPAR MA0220.1 (en, Drosophila melanogaster, UniProt P02836; PFM = [T/C]TAATT[A/G], PMID 18332042 Noyes et al. bacterial 1-hybrid). Corroborated by JASPAR MA0027.3 (human EN1, HT-SELEX, [T/C]AATTA) and by the primary structural paper: Fraenkel, Rould, Chambers & Pabo (1998) J Mol Biol 284:351-361, "Engrailed homeodomain-DNA complex at 2.2 A resolution", which states the protein is bound to "its optimal DNA site". Original 2.8 A structure: Kissinger et al. (1990) Cell 63:579-590 (PDB 1HDD).
controls.notes:
VERIFICATION. 3HDD exists and is "ENGRAILED HOMEODOMAIN DNA COMPLEX", 2.2 A X-ray, Drosophila melanogaster. Contents: protein entity 3 = 60 aa engrailed homeodomain, two copies, auth chains A and B (label C, D); DNA entity 1 = auth chain C, 5'-TTTTGCCATGTAATTACCTAA-3'; DNA entity 2 = auth chain D, 5'-ATTAGGTAATTACATGGCAAA-3'. Protein sequence above was taken verbatim from the fetched RCSB FASTA, not reconstructed. Both protein chains are the same entity/sequence, so chain A vs B is arbitrary.

MOTIF vs CRYSTAL. No conflict: the crystallised duplex contains TAATTA at top-strand positions 11-16, exactly matching the JASPAR consensus core. JASPAR MA0220.1 is 7 bp, [T/C]TAATT[A/G]; if a 7-mer is preferred use TTAATTA. Reported motif is the consensus, which here coincides with the crystallised site.

CONFOUNDS (read these before using as the "specific" positive control):
1. Stoichiometry. The asymmetric unit / deposited assembly contains TWO homeodomains and ONE 21-bp duplex (RCSB reports assembly 1 as "homo 2-mer, A2", C2). The biologically relevant engrailed HD-DNA complex is a 1:1 monomer on one TAAT core. TAATTA is self-complementary, so the two top/bottom-strand TAAT cores overlap and cannot both be fully occupied; the duplex also has 1-nt 5' overhangs and stacks end-to-end into a pseudo-continuous helix in the lattice, whose CCTAA|TTTTG junction regenerates a TAAT core. The second protein copy is therefore most likely on a lattice-generated / secondary site rather than a second independent site in the deposited duplex. If you predict 1 protein + 1 blunt duplex you will not reproduce the deposited coordinates residue-for-residue; if you predict 2 protein + 1 duplex you are modelling a crystallographic artefact. Recommend 1 chain + 1 duplex and compare only the specific interface.
2. Highly basic, small domain. 60 residues with 12 Arg + 7 Lys vs ~9 Asp/Glu (net roughly +10, pI ~11). Isolated homeodomains bind non-cognate DNA appreciably; engrailed HD discriminates cognate from random DNA by only ~1-2 orders of magnitude. This compresses the expected separation between this "specific" control and any "nonspecific_binder" control.
3. Low-information motif. Only ~6 bp are read by a monomer, and the core is AT-rich TAAT shared by essentially every homeodomain. A PAE-derived metric may not distinguish this from generic AT-rich/nonspecific engagement, and the motif is close to being a generic homeodomain half-site rather than a distinctive site.
4. Both grooves, and water-mediated specificity. Helix 3 reads the major groove, but the flexible N-terminal arm (E1-K2-R3-P4-R5-T6) inserts into the MINOR groove to read the TAAT core. That arm is disordered in the free protein (1ENH) and becomes ordered only on binding; AF3-class predictors commonly leave such arms low-confidence, which will inflate PAE for reasons unrelated to specificity. Additionally, Fraenkel et al. show Gln50 makes NO direct hydrogen bonds to DNA - specificity beyond the TAAT core is mediated by an ordered water network that these predictors do not model.
5. Minor bookkeeping: the RCSB HTML page renders DNA entity 2 as a 20-mer (…GGCAA) while the FASTA gives 21 nt (…GGCAAA); the FASTA/entity record was used here.

controls.label: TBP
controls.motif_source: JASPAR MA0108.3 (TBP, vertebrates; consensus TATAAAA — also MA0108.2, same core columns padded with uninformative flanks). Primary structure: Nikolov, Chen, Halay, Hisatake, Lee, Roeder, Burley, "Crystal structure of a human TATA box-binding protein/TATA element complex", PNAS 1996 (1CDW, 1.9 A).
controls.notes:
VERIFIED: 1CDW = "HUMAN TBP CORE DOMAIN COMPLEXED WITH DNA", 1.9 A, 1 protein entity + 2 DNA entities. Protein is entity chain C / auth chain A (Homo sapiens TBP), 179 aa — the C-terminal conserved core domain only; the N-terminal ~155 residues of full-length human TBP are absent from the construct. Sequence above taken verbatim from the RCSB FASTA, not from memory.

DNA: auth chain B = CTGCTATAAAAGGCTG, auth chain C = CAGCCTTTTATAGCAG. These are exact reverse complements, so it is a blunt 16-bp duplex (note: the two strands are separate polymer entities, so a modelling setup must supply both). The crystallised TATA element is TATAAAAG, which contains the JASPAR consensus TATAAAA exactly — consensus and crystallised site agree, no substitution needed.

CONFOUNDS / CAVEATS for use as a "specific" positive control:
1. MINOR-GROOVE READER. TBP is the textbook exception: it recognises the TATA box entirely through the minor groove via the concave underside of its saddle, using van der Waals/shape complementarity and 2'-deoxyribose contacts rather than major-groove base-edge hydrogen bonds. There are essentially no direct major-groove base-specific H-bonds. A PAE-derived interface metric that implicitly rewards canonical major-groove readout may score TBP poorly despite it being genuinely sequence-specific — this makes TBP a stress-test rather than an easy positive.
2. SEVERE DNA DISTORTION. Binding kinks the duplex by ~80 degrees (two ~45-degree kinks at the TATA ends), partially unwinds it, and inserts pairs of phenylalanines (F193/F210 and F284/F301 numbering of full-length TBP) between base pairs to pry the minor groove open. The bound DNA is far from B-form. AF3-class predictors are known to be biased toward B-form duplex DNA and may fail to reproduce this geometry, which can depress or inflate PAE at the interface for reasons unrelated to specificity.
3. Pseudo-two-fold internal symmetry: the core is a single chain built from two direct repeats, and it binds the (non-palindromic) TATA box in a defined polarity determined by the flanking sequence. Docking polarity is a genuine failure mode; a flipped-but-plausible pose is possible.
4. Modest net positive charge: K+R = 29, D+E = 13, net +16 over 179 aa (16% basic). Not extreme, but the DNA-binding saddle surface is basic, and TBP does have measurable affinity for non-TATA DNA in vitro (TATA-independent binding is documented), so it is not a "zero background" specific binder.
5. Biologically TBP functions within TFIID and its DNA binding in vivo is modulated by TAF1, NC2 and Mot1; free TBP also self-associates into an autoinhibitory dimer in solution. The 1:1 core-domain/TATA complex crystallised here is nonetheless a well-established physiological binding mode, so monomer modelling is defensible — but the isolated core is a construct, not the cellular species.
6. The motif is short (7 bp) and low-complexity/AT-only, so any negative control built by shuffling must avoid accidentally regenerating an A/T tract that TBP would still bind.

controls.label: Sac7d
controls.motif_source: No motif — non-sequence-specific. Robinson et al., Nature 392:202-205 (1998), doi:10.1038/32455 ("The hyperthermophile chromosomal protein Sac7d sharply kinks DNA"); McAfee/Edmondson/Shriver, Biochemistry 1996 (doi:10.1021/bi952555q) equilibrium binding shows no sequence preference; Nadassy/Wodak review on non-sequence-specific recognition. No JASPAR matrix exists (archaeal chromatin protein, not a TF).
controls.notes:
VERIFIED against RCSB. Entry 1AZP = "Hyperthermophile chromosomal protein Sac7d bound with kinked DNA duplex", X-ray, 1.6 A, Sulfolobus acidocaldarius (taxid 2285). Two entities: protein entity is label chain C / auth chain A (66 aa, sequence taken verbatim from https://www.rcsb.org/fasta/entry/1AZP); DNA is a self-complementary 8-mer d(GCGATCGC) as auth chains B and C. NOTE the auth/label chain relabelling — auth C is a DNA strand, not the protein; the protein is auth A.

Confounders for use as a non-specific control:
(1) Extremely basic protein. 11 Lys + 2 Arg in 66 residues, pI ~10; binding is driven by ~6 Lys-phosphate salt bridges plus a hydrophobic minor-groove surface. It will adhere to essentially any duplex, and to ssDNA/RNA too. This is the point of the control, but it means a predictor could score a confident interface for any DNA sequence you hand it — which is the desired behaviour for a "non-specific" class but makes it a weak discriminator if your metric only asks "is there an interface".
(2) Reads the MINOR groove, not the major groove, and kinks DNA ~61 deg via Val26/Met29 intercalation. Predictors trained largely on major-groove readers may model the DNA geometry poorly; a bad PAE here could reflect failure to reproduce a sharply kinked duplex rather than absence of specificity.
(3) Not perfectly indifferent: intercalation shows mild step preference (CG or TT steps), and the crystallised site GCGATCGC contains such a step. Reported binding-affinity variation with sequence is small (a few-fold) but non-zero, so "zero specificity" is an approximation, not a strict truth.
(4) Short DNA. Only 8 bp of duplex in the crystal; terminal base pairs are frayed/end-effect prone, so PAE on a re-prediction with a longer duplex is not directly comparable to the deposited structure.
(5) Monomer, so no oligomeric-state problem (unlike obligate dimers) — one protein chain per duplex. Crystal packing does place symmetry-related copies on the DNA ends, but the biological unit is 1 protein : 1 duplex.
(6) Sac7d/Sso7d is the parent scaffold for engineered "Affitin" binders; make sure any literature hit you use describes wild-type Sac7d and not an affinity-matured variant.
(7) cognate_motif intentionally the empty string.

controls.label: Ubiquitin
controls.motif_source: N/A — no cognate DNA site. Structure citation: Vijay-Kumar S, Bugg CE, Cook WJ, "Structure of ubiquitin refined at 1.8 A resolution", J Mol Biol 1987 (PDB 1UBQ).
controls.notes:
VERIFIED against RCSB: 1UBQ = "STRUCTURE OF UBIQUITIN REFINED AT 1.8 ANGSTROMS RESOLUTION", X-ray 1.8 A, deposited 1987. Entity counts: protein 1, DNA 0, RNA 0; polymer_composition = "homomeric protein"; selected_polymer_entity_types = protein only. So is_protein_dna_cocrystal is correctly false — apo, single chain A, Homo sapiens, 76 aa, sequence taken verbatim from https://www.rcsb.org/fasta/entry/1UBQ (header ">1UBQ_1|Chain A|UBIQUITIN|Homo sapiens (9606)"). Note 1UBQ chain A models residues 1-76 with the C-terminal 76 present, so the fetched FASTA and the observed coordinates agree closely (the last couple of residues of the LRGG tail are the least ordered part of the model).

Suitability as a negative control — good, with caveats:
- No known dsDNA-binding activity. Ubiquitin is a post-translational modifier; it has no recognised nucleic-acid-binding domain, and literature searching turns up only cases where ubiquitin is *delivered to* nucleic acids or chromatin by other proteins (e.g. DTX3L-RD binds single-stranded DNA/RNA via KH/RRM domains and esterifies Ub onto 3'-terminal adenosine; H2A/H2B ubiquitylation on nucleosomes). In all such cases the DNA/chromatin affinity resides in the ligase or histone, not in ubiquitin itself. This is a genuine nonbinder, not a weak binder.
- Charge: ubiquitin is close to charge-neutral at pH 7 (7 Lys + 4 Arg vs 6 Glu + 5-6 Asp; pI ~6.8), so it should NOT stick to DNA electrostatically. This is a real advantage over many small "inert" controls (e.g. lysozyme, protamine-like peptides) that are strongly basic and would give false-positive interfaces.
- Monomeric and folded as deposited — no obligate-oligomer artefact, no need to reconstruct a biological assembly.
- Confounders to keep in mind: (1) 76 aa is small, so any PAE-derived interface metric will be computed over far fewer residue pairs than for a typical TF-DNA complex; if the metric is not size-normalised, ubiquitin is not size-matched to the specific-binder arm of the panel. (2) Ubiquitin is one of the most over-represented sequences in the PDB and in every training set, so intra-chain pLDDT/PAE will be extremely confident; make sure the metric isolates the protein-DNA cross-block and is not contaminated by intramolecular confidence. (3) Ubiquitin does have well-characterised protein-protein interaction surfaces (the Ile44 hydrophobic patch, the Ile36 patch) and appears in the PDB in many chromatin/DNA-repair complexes; a predictor could plausibly hallucinate a plausible-looking interface simply because ubiquitin co-occurs with DNA-proximal machinery in training data. (4) The flexible C-terminal L73-R74-G75-G76 tail (with R72/R74) is the one locally basic, disordered feature and is the most likely site of a spurious predicted DNA contact — worth inspecting per-residue if this control fails.
- cognate_motif deliberately empty; motif_source not applicable.

controls.label: GFP
controls.motif_source: Not applicable (nonbinder). Structure citation: Ormo M, Cubitt AB, Kallio K, Gross LA, Tsien RY, Remington SJ. "Crystal structure of the Aequorea victoria green fluorescent protein." Science 273:1392-1395 (1996). UniProt P42212.
controls.notes:
VERIFIED via RCSB REST API. 1EMA exists and is "GREEN FLUORESCENT PROTEIN FROM AEQUOREA VICTORIA", 1.9 A X-ray, Ormo et al. Science 1996. polymer_entity_count_protein = 1, polymer_entity_count_dna = 0, polymer_entity_count_rna = 0; selected_polymer_entity_types = "Protein (only)". Single polymer chain, auth_asym_id = A. No DNA, no nucleic acid of any kind, so is_protein_dna_cocrystal = false and cognate_motif is empty. GFP has no reported sequence-specific or non-specific DNA binding; it is the canonical inert negative-control protein in the literature.

CONFOUND / CAVEAT 1 (IMPORTANT, must be handled before folding): the sequence above is the exact PDB one-letter code and contains a non-standard 'X' at position 65. That X is the CRO chromophore, a single modified residue formed by autocatalytic cyclisation/oxidation of the Thr65-Tyr66-Gly67 tripeptide (1EMA is the S65T variant, so 65 is Thr, not Ser). AF3-class predictors will either reject 'X' or model it as UNK, which will locally distort the barrel and could perturb PAE. For prediction input, replace the single X with the three residues TYG, giving a 238-residue standard-alphabet chain (...LVTTF-TYG-VQCFSRY...). Decide and record which form was used; the 236-mer with X is NOT a valid model input.

CAVEAT 2: 1EMA is not strictly wild type. RCSB annotates the entity as carrying the S65T chromophore-environment mutation plus a Q80R substitution (a well-known PCR artefact present in most GFP clones). Neither affects the DNA-binding-negative status.

CAVEAT 3 (supports its use as a control): computed composition of the deposited chain is K+R = 27, D+E = 34, net formal charge about -7 at neutral pH (GFP pI ~5.7). The protein is net ANIONIC, so there is no basic-patch artefact that would make it stick to DNA electrostatically. Fold is an 11-strand beta-barrel with a central helix; no HTH, zinc finger, beta-hairpin, or any recognised DNA-binding architecture; no exposed positively charged groove.

CAVEAT 4: biological unit. A. victoria GFP is essentially monomeric (weak, ~100 uM Kd dimerisation via a hydrophobic patch A206/L221/F223 seen in some crystal forms). The 1EMA asymmetric unit contains a single chain, so a monomeric prediction is physically reasonable. No obligate-oligomer problem.

CAVEAT 5 (benchmark hygiene, not biology): GFP is one of the most over-represented folds in the PDB and in any structure predictor's training data. Its monomer will be predicted with near-perfect confidence, so any protein-DNA PAE metric computed for a GFP+DNA complex reflects the model's willingness to place an unrelated DNA duplex, not fold uncertainty. That is what you want from a negative control, but note that the intra-protein PAE will be anomalously low compared with other panel members. Also, because there is no cognate DNA, you must specify which decoy duplex is paired with GFP; use the same decoy sequence(s) across all nonbinder entries so the comparison is controlled.

table1_verification.overall:
HOW ACCESS WAS OBTAINED (read this before retiring the flag). bioRxiv returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch on every direct URL (v1, .full, .full.pdf), under both the 10.1101 and the actual 10.64898 DOI prefix. Europe PMC has the preprint indexed as PPR1213115 but abstract-only (fullTextXML = 404). Semantic Scholar rate-limited. I reached the text through the r.jina.ai text-extraction proxy on https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.04.27.720408v1.full-text. Two caveats on the strength of that evidence: (a) I never saw the raw bytes myself — Bash/curl was denied, so every read passed through WebFetch's summarizing model over the proxy's rendering; (b) one proxy read said the Table 1 grid itself was not in the extracted markdown and that the sequences it could quote came from the Methods paragraph enumerating the targets, while another read presented a 16-row Table 1. So what I verified is the paper's own name-to-sequence assignments as they appear in the extracted full text, which may be the Methods enumeration rather than the Table 1 grid per se; the strings and labels are the same either way.

WHY I BELIEVE THE READS. I ran a decoy-controlled presence check: 12 strings, 4 fabricated (TTGCATCAGCTA, CACGTGACGTCA, AAACCCTAACCC, CCCTAACCCTAA — the last two deliberately telomere-adjacent). All 4 decoys were correctly reported ABSENT and all 8 real strings PRESENT with their labels quoted ("GGGGATTCCCCC (NFkB-site)", "GCGTAAACAA (FKH-site)", etc.). That rules out blanket confirmation of whatever I fed in, which was my main worry. An earlier independent read quoted the core-six sentence verbatim, including "CAGCAGCAGCAG (CAG)", "TGAGGAGAGGAG (PRNP-site)", "CGTATAAACG (TBP-site)", "GGGCTTGCGA (Oct4-gRNA2)".

All 9 questioned sequences plus PRNP match the paper's text character for character, including lengths (10-mers vs 12-mers). ONE DISCREPANCY TO NOTE, not a transcription error in the repo: GGGCTTGCGA appears in the paper labelled both as Oct4-gRNA2 and as Dux4-gRNA2 (confirmed on two separate reads, and an independent web-search snippet described GGGCTTGCGA as "Dux4-gRNA2"). Either the paper reuses one sequence under two names or its table has a copy-paste error. The repo's Oct4gRNA2 -> GGGCTTGCGA mapping is one of the two labelings the paper itself carries, so I would keep a note rather than silently accept it as unambiguous.

SEPARATE AND WEAKER EVIDENCE — canonical-motif plausibility from my own knowledge, independent of the paper. This is NOT verification of the transcription; it only says the strings are chemically sensible for the named factors. TBP CGTATAAACG contains TATAAA, the canonical TATA box — plausible. NFkB GGGGATTCCCCC fits the kB consensus GGGRNNYYCC and closely resembles the classic palindromic GGGGATTCCCC element — plausible (note the repo string is 12 nt with five terminal Cs, i.e. GGGGATTCCCCC, which is a symmetric extension rather than the textbook 11-mer; worth an eyeball). P53 AGACATGTCT is a self-complementary 10-mer with a CATG core, consistent with the RRRCWWGYYY half-site grammar — plausible. FKH GCGTAAACAA contains GTAAACA, the forkhead consensus — plausible. HD GCTTAATTAGCG contains the palindromic TAATTA homeodomain core — plausible. Tbox AGGTGTGAAG contains AGGTGTGA, the T-box/Brachyury half-site core — plausible. HSTelo AGGGTTAGGGTT is two TTAGGG human telomeric repeats in frame — plausible. CAGCAGCAGCAG is a trivial four-unit CAG repeat. Oct4gRNA2 and PRNP are genomic guide-derived sites with no canonical consensus, so plausibility says nothing about them either way.

BOTTOM LINE. I would downgrade the flag from UNVERIFIED to "verified against the bioRxiv full text via a text-extraction proxy, decoy-controlled, raw source never directly inspected", and I would keep the Oct4-gRNA2/Dux4-gRNA2 label collision recorded next to the Oct4gRNA2 entry. If the pre-flight gate is cheap to keep, a human eyeball on the actual PDF Table 1 is still the thing that closes this properly.
